methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort study from VA Corporate Data Warehouse with 107 patients; Kaplan-Meier analysis for OS appropriate. Manual chart abstraction for clinical parameters by single reviewer limits inter-rater reliability assessment. Subgroup analyses conducted but some subgroups small (e.g., Child-Pugh B n=26); wide confidence intervals reflect precision limitations. Sensitivity analysis limited to HIMALAYA-eligible patients strengthens findings but post-hoc selection.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Real-world cohort study with direct clinical relevance to treatment decisions in unresectable HCC, particularly for Child-Pugh B patients (24% of cohort) typically excluded from RCTs. Demonstrates STRIDE safety/efficacy in broader population than HIMALAYA trial. Addresses practice-relevant questions about prior locoregional therapy, viral etiology, and advanced liver dysfunction that affect real-world patient management.

reporting_quality.justification: Follows STROBE guidelines with clear methods, baseline characteristics, and outcome reporting. Acknowledges VA population limitations and selection bias from non-randomized design. However, lacks explicit data availability statement; CDW data access restricted to VA system. Manual abstraction methods not fully specified; inter-rater reliability not assessed. Supplementary tables provide detailed AE frequencies.

novelty_literature.justification: Extends HIMALAYA trial findings to real-world VA population with prior non-systemic therapy (72%), Child-Pugh B function (24%), and diverse etiologies. Addresses acknowledged gap between RCT populations and routine practice. Findings largely confirm trial results rather than discover novel mechanisms, representing incremental clinical evidence for broader population applicability.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear introduction contextualizing gaps in trial-derived knowledge, transparent methods, comprehensive results organized by subgroups, and thoughtful discussion comparing with HIMALAYA and other real-world studies. Limitations section thoroughly acknowledges VA population demographics, missing EMR data, and short follow-up period. Figures effectively communicate Kaplan-Meier curves.

key_strengths: Addresses clinically important gap: demonstrates STRIDE safety in Child-Pugh B patients typically excluded from RCTs; only 3/22 Grade 3-4 AEs in CP-B subset
Large national cohort with diverse demographics allowing detailed subgroup analyses; comprehensive manual chart abstraction for clinical covariates
Real-world data validate trial findings in broader population: median OS 12.6 mo in HIMALAYA-eligible subgroup comparable to trial (16.4 mo)
Transparent comparison with HIMALAYA and prior VA cohorts; sensitivity analysis strengthens evidence
key_concerns: Single-center manual chart review by one abstractor limits inter-rater reliability; EMR data quality variable and some clinical parameters missing
Retrospective design and non-random treatment assignment introduce selection bias; short follow-up for some patients truncates OS estimates
VA population 100% male, older, higher comorbidity burden limits generalizability to broader US population
No contemporary control arm; comparisons use historical HIMALAYA trial data rather than within-study comparators
Small sample sizes in Child-Pugh B (n=26) and certain etiology subgroups limit precision of effect estimates
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality real-world evidence paper addressing practice-relevant questions about immunotherapy in challenging subpopulations. Methodologically sound for observational study type with appropriate analyses and transparent limitations. Suitable for Tier 3 journals emphasizing clinically relevant translational evidence.
